correctness.rationale: PASS: The unsigned vertex-edge incidence B over characteristic two gives F=B^TB with no diagonal self-loops and L=BB^T. Connectedness gives imB=W (coordinate sum 0) and ker B^T=〈1〉. For all-even clique sizes L=Σ_i J_{mi} on tensor factors, with each J²=0; characteristic-two cancellation yields L²=0 and F³=0. Each factor (F2^{mi},J_{mi}) has one contractible 2-block and mi-2 trivial homology blocks; tensor contracting homotopies imply total homology dimension H=∏(mi-2), so rankL=(N-H)/2. Since 1∈W, kerL⊂W and 1∈L(W) (explicit unit⊗all-ones vector, r>=2), rankF=N-2 and rankF²=rankL-2. These ranks exactly yield all three Jordan multiplicities and counts C_t=q^{dim kerF^t}-q^{dim kerF^{t-1}}. With any odd factor, the tensor of e0+e1 in that factor and all-ones elsewhere is a sum-zero Laplacian eigenvector with eigenvalue 1, giving B^Tv a nonzero F-fixed edge state. Independent GF2 line-graph matrices were constructed directly for nine even/odd small tuples and reproduced ranks; no finite test extrapolation to arbitrary field sizes or factors. The claimed exceptional nilpotency index two for K2□K2 follows from rankF²=0.

value.rationale: PASS: Characteristic-two edge-neighbor dynamics on Cartesian clique/Hamming graphs is a natural linear cellular automaton with a meaningful structural parity boundary. The theorem identifies exactly when every state is extinguished, gives an all-alphabet Jordan census and sharp extinction times, and introduces the nontrivial tensor-homology factor H. The all-binary cube subcase is credited as known rather than claimed new. This is a genuine infinite family classification, not merely a code-table recomputation.

final_claim: For G=K_{m_1}□...□K_{m_r}, r>=2, mi>=2, on the line graph L(G) over any finite characteristic-two field, the open-neighborhood neighbor-sum map F is nilpotent iff all mi are even. In that case F³=0, rankF=N-2 and rankF²=(N-H)/2-2, giving the stated complete Jordan multiplicities and exact first-zero populations; any odd mi supplies a nonzero fixed vector.
